newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Airlines says unit board resigns. [CORRECTED 15:54 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Canadian Airlines says unit board resigns. [CORRECTED 15:54 GMT]

text.p: Canadian Airlines Corp said on Friday that all members of the board of its operating company, Canadian Airlines International Ltd, have resigned.
The resignations were recommended by legal counsel to the board and reflect the directors' concerns over growing personal liability, the parent company said.

"Notwithstanding this event, I believe that the company and its unions are very focused on solving the issues facing us. Wednesday's discussions with unions raised a number of ideas which are being evaluated and meetings will continue within a week," president Kevin Benson said in a statement.
The board of Canadian Airlines Corp is unchanged.

Until a new board is constituted, the affairs of Canadian Airlines International will be directed by shareholders, Canadian Airlines Corp and Aurora Airline Investments Inc, a wholly owned subsidiary of AMR Corp.
Calgary-based Canadian Airlines Corp has a 67-percent (corrects from 70-percent) ownership interest and 75-percent voting interest in Canadian Airines International.
Fort Worth, Texas-based AMR, the parent of American Airlines, has a 33-percent ownership interest and 25-percent voting interest in Canadian Airlines International.
